title: Pidgeotto’s 60-Mile Prey Flight
premise: Pidgeotto immobilizes prey with its claws, then can carry it over 60 miles back to its nest.
audiencePromise: Follow Pidgeotto’s hunt from its aerial search to its startlingly distant nest run.
openLoop: How can a sky-high scout turn one catch into a 60-mile carry?
payoff: Pidgeotto first renders prey immobile, then can carry prey such as Exeggcute over 60 miles to its nest.
engagementQuestion: Sharp-eyed scout or clawed hunter: which defines Pidgeotto?

voice.instructions: Use a tense, documentary tone. Start sharp and urgent, then widen with awe as the route expands. Keep each line clean, direct, and slightly incredulous.

scenes.headline: CAUGHT HERE. NEST 60 MILES AWAY.
scenes.narration: Caught by Pidgeotto? Your trip home exceeds sixty miles.
scenes.caption: CAUGHT → CARRIED → OVER 60 MILES

scenes.headline: IT CIRCLES FOR PREY
scenes.narration: It circles slowly, keeping a sharp lookout for prey.
scenes.caption: A SLOW CIRCULAR SEARCH

scenes.headline: PREY MOVEMENTS STAND OUT
scenes.narration: However high it flies, Pidgeotto spots its prey's movements.
scenes.caption: IT CAN DISTINGUISH PREY MOVEMENTS

scenes.headline: CLAWS MAKE PREY IMMOBILE
scenes.narration: Well-developed claws render prey immobile before Pidgeotto carries it.
scenes.caption: FIRST: PREY STOPS MOVING

scenes.headline: EXEGGCUTE CAN MAKE THE TRIP
scenes.narration: Exeggcute is named as prey carried over sixty miles.
scenes.caption: EXEGGCUTE → NEST: OVER 60 MILES
